## US moves diplomats, Trump floats new Iran military operation
Axios reported that US intelligence assesses Iran has “substantially increased” efforts to target American diplomats and officials, with some alleged lethal plots reaching “advanced stages.” The intelligence was cited as one reason for reductions in US diplomatic personnel across several Middle Eastern countries
The US is quietly moving some diplomats and family members out of Lebanon, the UAE, Qatar and Jordan amid concerns over further regional escalation, CNN reported Friday, citing multiple sources and a State Department official.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said oil exports from the Persian Gulf had surpassed pre-war levels despite Iran’s attempts to disrupt energy shipments.
Masoud Pezeshkian is expected at the eighth Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit in Moscow on Oct. 27. Abbas Araghchi said Pezeshkian would travel to Moscow and meet Vladimir Putin next week.
The United States could launch another military operation against Iran unless Tehran reaches an agreement with Washington, President Donald Trump said Friday at a rally in Florida.
IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said most technical preparations needed to verify Iran’s nuclear activities have been completed and the agency is “ready.” He said there could be no lasting solution without a diplomatic agreement.
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan called for the Iran war to be addressed through dialogue and diplomacy and urged the full resumption of safe and unrestricted passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

## Iran military chief says US warships will not be allowed into Persian Gulf
Iran will not allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf “under any circumstances,” Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ali Abdollahi said on Saturday, according to the IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency.
“We will not, under any circumstances or at any time, allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf,” Abdollahi said.
He claimed Iran’s armed forces had rendered the US Navy ineffective and said American forces were no longer able to approach waters around the Persian Gulf or Iran’s territorial waters.
“The US president can only dream of their military and army entering the Persian Gulf again,” Abdollahi said, Tasnim reported.
Oct 24, 2026, 04:41 GMT+1
## UK foreign secretary says Iran war has gone on ‘too long’
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Friday that the Iran war and Tehran’s attacks on shipping were driving up energy and food bills and inflation in Britain, calling for diplomacy to bring the conflict to a lasting end.
“The Iran war and Iran’s attacks on shipping are raising energy bills, raising food bills, raising inflation,” Miliband told reporters in Istanbul, where he was attending talks with European and regional counterparts.
“Diplomacy, dialogue and de-escalation has to be the answer to this conflict,” he said.
“Frankly, this conflict has gone on too long. The British people have suffered too much from it, and we cannot afford months more of it,” Miliband added. The Istanbul meeting brought together foreign ministers from Britain, France, Germany and Italy with counterparts from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt.
Oct 24, 2026, 04:20 GMT+1
## UN Iran rapporteur says war intensified repression
UN Special Rapporteur on Iran Mai Sato said the war intensified repression inside Iran, with protesters portrayed as agents of hostile countries and executions continuing throughout the period, in a post on X Friday.
“The war not only failed to reduce the intensity of repression, but intensified it,” Sato said.
“What these reports have in common is impunity,” she said, referring to three recent UN reports on human rights in Iran. Sato said she was unaware of investigations by Iranian authorities into killings by their forces, while the United States and Israel had not published findings on their attacks.
She called for an end to hostilities through diplomacy, a halt to executions, the release of people detained for exercising their rights and independent investigations into deaths.
Oct 24, 2026, 03:12 GMT+1
## US moves diplomats, families from Middle East posts amid Iran escalation fears - CNN
The United States is quietly moving some diplomats and family members out of posts in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Jordan as concerns grow over further regional escalation involving Iran, CNN reported Friday, citing multiple sources and a State Department official.
The State Department confirmed the four countries would see temporary staffing changes under “restricted operations,” but said the embassies had not formally changed status.
The moves have not been publicly announced and come after Washington ordered non-emergency personnel and all family members to leave Saudi Arabia in response to increased attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.
CNN reported that some of those now leaving had only recently returned to their posts after being ordered out during the height of the Iran war.
The adjustments also come as President Donald Trump has suggested the United States could relaunch strikes against Iran after the midterm elections and Israel has unsuccessfully pushed for more immediate action, CNN reported.
Oct 24, 2026, 02:51 GMT+1
## Iran says it has not suspended nuclear safeguards obligations
Iran has not abandoned or suspended its safeguards obligations under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, but military attacks have changed the security conditions under which they can be implemented, Iran’s UN Ambassador Gholamhossein Darzi said Friday.
Darzi made the remarks during the UN General Assembly’s debate on the International Atomic Energy Agency’s annual report in New York.
“Iran has neither abandoned nor suspended its safeguards obligations,” Darzi said, adding that military attacks had changed the security conditions under which those obligations could be implemented.
He said Iran had been a party to the NPT since 1970 and had remained committed to its international obligations, while its peaceful nuclear facilities had been subjected to military attacks.
Darzi also said the IAEA had acknowledged that inspectors left Iran for security reasons and that those concerns could not be ignored when seeking their return.
Oct 24, 2026, 02:34 GMT+1
## QatarEnergy in talks to buy US LNG as Iran war disrupts Hormuz shipping - Reuters
QatarEnergy is in talks to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas a year from Woodside Energy’s Louisiana LNG project as the Iran war continues to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reported Friday, citing three people familiar with the negotiations.
A potential agreement could run for 15 to 20 years, with LNG supplied from Woodside’s 16.5-million-ton-per-year Louisiana facility, which is under construction.
QatarEnergy has been buying LNG on the US spot market to meet customer commitments because the ongoing blockage of the Strait of Hormuz has sharply curtailed shipping, Reuters reported.
The talks come after Cheniere Energy agreed to supply QatarEnergy with 4 million tons of LNG annually under a long-term deal, split between its Sabine Pass facility in Louisiana and Corpus Christi terminal in Texas.
Reuters also reported Thursday that QatarEnergy was in advanced talks with Venture Global to buy at least 3 million tons of LNG annually under a long-term agreement.

## Video: Trump says US may carry out another military operation against Iran
US President Donald Trump said Friday that Washington may carry out another military operation against Iran.
“We may do another little Epic Fury,” Trump said at a rally in Fort Myers, Florida.
Earlier Friday, Trump said the United States could end the war quickly but questioned whether it should seek a swift conclusion or allow the conflict to gradually wind down.

## Iran, Russia, China among 12 states condemning attacks on nuclear facilities
Iran, Russia, China and nine other countries said Friday that nuclear facilities under International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards and dedicated to peaceful purposes should never be attacked or threatened with attack, Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported.
The joint statement was issued at the UN General Assembly’s First Committee by Belarus, Burkina Faso, China, Cuba, Eritrea, Iran, Nicaragua, Niger, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan and Zimbabwe.
The countries said attacks or threats against nuclear facilities violate the principles of the UN Charter, international law and the IAEA statute and could have serious consequences for nuclear safety and security.
They also warned that attacks could result in the release of radioactive material, with severe consequences for civilians and long-term environmental damage.
“We reiterate that nuclear facilities should never and under no circumstances be subject to attack or threat of attack,” the statement said.
Iran’s ambassador to the UN, Gholamhossein Darzi, read the eight-point statement at the committee meeting, according to IRNA.
Oct 24, 2026, 01:24 GMT+1
## US intel warns Iran assassination plots have reached ‘advanced stages’ - Axios
Iran has “substantially increased” efforts to target US diplomats and officials in the Middle East and beyond, with lethal plots reaching “advanced stages,” Axios reported Friday, citing a US intelligence memo.
The Oct. 23 memo to Secretary of State Marco Rubio does not identify specific targets or describe the nature of the alleged plots, but says the underlying intelligence has been shared with senior State Department officials.
Axios said the intelligence was one reason the State Department has been reducing personnel at several US embassies across the Middle East.
A US official said Friday that personnel were being reduced at embassies in the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon, Qatar and Jordan because of threats from Iran-backed Houthis and alleged Iran plots.
Earlier this week, the State Department ordered family members and nonessential personnel to leave the US Embassy in Riyadh and consulates in Jeddah and Dhahran.
